title: hsk30: grading Chinese text against either document called HSK 3.0
description:
“HSK 3.0” names two different official documents: the GF0025-2021 national grading standard, in force since July 2021, and the examination syllabus published in November 2025, the basis of the HSK 3.0 exam from 13 December 2026. They assign different levels to 41.5% of the words and 40.7% of the characters they share, and grading real texts against one rather than the other changes the level of roughly half of them.

This release contains a dependency-free Python library that grades Chinese text against either document and records which (also on npm as a JavaScript port with identical grades); a validated extraction of the 2025 examination syllabus from the official 406-page PDF, with all 11,000 entries including homograph readings; a registry of identifiers and a one-file convention for declaring which HSK document a dataset encodes, with a checker; an aligned corpus of 102 graded readers with per-word pinyin and gloss plus a disjoint 30-text held-out split; and WriteToLevel, a difficulty-controlled generation benchmark in which the grader serves as the metric rather than as the source of labels, packaged for Inspect and lm-evaluation-harness.

Software is MIT licensed; the corpus is CC BY 4.0 and carries a datasheet disclosing LLM-assisted authorship.
